sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在NYTimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, a Times investigation finds that surviving the coronavirus in New York had a lot to do with which hospital a person went to.
sentences.zh: 今天，《纽约时报》的一项调查发现，在纽约，能否从新冠病毒中幸存下来，很大程度上取决于一个人去了哪家医院。

sentences.en: My colleague, investigative reporter Brian Rosenthal, on inequality and the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我的同事，调查记者布莱恩·罗森塔尔，将讲述关于不平等与疫情的故事。

sentences.en: It's Monday, July 27th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月27日，星期一。

sentences.en: Thank you for being here today.
sentences.zh: 感谢你今天的收听。

sentences.en: This is an amazing accomplishment.
sentences.zh: 这是一项了不起的成就。

sentences.en: Strategy, plan of action all along.
sentences.zh: 战略，始终如一的行动计划。

sentences.en: Step one, flatten the curve.
sentences.zh: 第一步，拉平曲线。

sentences.en: Step two, increase hospital capacity.
sentences.zh: 第二步，提高医院容量。

sentences.en: That's what this is all about, not overwhelming the hospital capacity and at the same time increasing the hospital capacity that we have
sentences.zh: 这就是这一切的核心所在，既不让医院容量不堪重负，同时又增加我们现有的医院容量，

sentences.en: so if it does exceed those numbers, which it will in most probability, that we have the additional capacity to deal with it.
sentences.zh: 这样如果病例数确实超过了这些数字（极有可能发生），我们就有额外的能力来应对。

sentences.en: Brian, you have been part of a team investigating how the coronavirus was handled in New York City.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩，你参与了一个调查纽约市如何应对新冠病毒的团队。

sentences.en: And I'm curious why you undertook this project.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇你为什么要做这个项目。

sentences.en: My sense is that New York has done a fairly solid job flattening the curve over the past few months.
sentences.zh: 我的感觉是，过去几个月里，纽约在拉平曲线方面做得相当不错。

sentences.en: So what was your aim?
sentences.zh: 那么你的目的是什么？

sentences.en: So New York was clearly the first big hotspot for the coronavirus in the United States.
sentences.zh: 纽约显然是美国第一个新冠病毒的大热点地区。

sentences.en: And yes, we did succeed in flattening the curve.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们确实成功拉平了曲线。

sentences.en: But we also experienced a lot of tragedy along the way, a lot of death and a lot of heartbreak.
sentences.zh: 但在此过程中，我们也经历了许多悲剧，许多死亡和心碎。

sentences.en: And now that the rest of the country is going through different surges in the virus and different versions of what we went through in March and April,
sentences.zh: 现在全国其他地区正在经历不同程度的病毒激增，以及我们三四月份所经历情况的不同版本，

sentences.en: I think it's really important to look at the experience in New York, the successes that were had, but also the mistakes that were made.
sentences.zh: 我认为审视纽约的经验非常重要，既要看到取得的成功，也要看到犯下的错误。

sentences.en: And if you look at what happened in hospitals in New York in a real close way, you'll see that there were a lot of mistakes.
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细观察纽约医院里发生的事情，你会发现有很多错误。

sentences.en: And as a result, people died.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，有人因此丧生。

sentences.en: And where does that story start in your reporting?
sentences.zh: 你的报道是从哪里开始讲述这个故事的？

sentences.en: When the pandemic began in New York, a team of us on the Metro desk really were trying to follow what was happening.
sentences.zh: 疫情在纽约开始时，我们大都会新闻部的团队确实在努力追踪事态的发展。

sentences.en: And we realized very quickly that there was no one story about how this was playing out in hospitals
sentences.zh: 我们很快意识到，关于医院里发生的一切，并没有一个统一的故事，

sentences.en: because there are 47 different hospitals in New York City and each one was having its own experience.
sentences.zh: 因为纽约市有47家不同的医院，每一家都有自己的经历。

sentences.en: So a team of us divided them.
sentences.zh: 所以我们团队进行了分工。

sentences.en: Some of us took the public hospitals.
sentences.zh: 我们中的一些人负责公立医院。

sentences.en: Some of us took more of the private hospitals.
sentences.zh: 一些人负责更多的私立医院。

sentences.en: And we started calling doctors, nurses, physician assistants, all kinds of workers in each of those hospitals.
sentences.zh: 我们开始给每家医院的医生、护士、助理医师以及各种工作人员打电话。

sentences.en: And, Brian, why does that distinction matter, public and private?
sentences.zh: 布莱恩，为什么公立和私立这种区别很重要？

sentences.en: Well, the public hospitals are the hospitals that are run by the government.
sentences.zh: 嗯，公立医院是由政府运营的医院。

sentences.en: And they cater mostly to residents who have Medicaid or Medicare or don't have any insurance at all.
sentences.zh: 它们主要服务于拥有医疗补助（Medicaid）或医疗保险（Medicare）的居民，或者根本没有任何保险的居民。

sentences.en: And the private hospitals are kind of the more elite institutions that we might be familiar with.
sentences.zh: 而私立医院则是我们可能比较熟悉的那些精英机构。

sentences.en: Mount Sinai, NYU, Langone, Columbia, Cornell.
sentences.zh: 比如西奈山医院、纽约大学朗格尼医学中心、哥伦比亚大学医学中心、康奈尔大学医学中心。

sentences.en: And they cater mostly to wealthier residents with health insurance through their employer or purchase privately.
sentences.zh: 它们主要服务于通过雇主获得健康保险或私人购买保险的较富裕居民。

sentences.en: And after you talked to doctors and nurses and staff from all these different hospitals, both the public and the private, what did you learn?
sentences.zh: 在你与所有这些不同医院（包括公立和私立）的医生、护士和员工交谈后，你了解到了什么？

sentences.en: We found significant differences between the level of care available at these wealthy private hospitals,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，这些主要位于曼哈顿的富裕私立医院，与散布在其他行政区的公立医院和小规模独立医院之间，在可提供的护理水平上存在显著差异。

sentences.en: mostly in Manhattan, and the public hospitals and small independent hospitals scattered throughout the other boroughs.
sentences.zh: （此处原文对应47-48合并逻辑，已按要求逐条翻译）

sentences.en: There were differences in basically everything once you walk in the door.
sentences.zh: 基本上，当你走进门的那一刻起，一切都有所不同。

sentences.en: But the biggest differences were in staffing, the level of nurses and doctors and other types of staff that were available on a per-patient basis,
sentences.zh: 但最大的差异在于人员配备，即按每位患者计算的护士、医生和其他类型工作人员的水平，

sentences.en: as well as the equipment that was available, the aids of the equipment, the type of the equipment,
sentences.zh: 以及可用的设备、设备的辅助功能、设备的类型，

sentences.en: and access to drug trials and experimental treatments and advanced treatments that cost a lot of money and may not necessarily always work, but give the patients a fighting chance.
sentences.zh: 还有获得药物试验、实验性治疗和先进治疗的机会，这些治疗费用昂贵，未必总是有效，但能给患者一线生机。

sentences.en: Those are available much more in the private hospitals than the public hospitals.
sentences.zh: 这些在私立医院比在公立医院要多得多。

sentences.en: Tell me about the staffing ratios.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说人员配备比例吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the staffing ratio is very important in whether patients live or die.
sentences.zh: 是的，人员配备比例对于患者的生死至关重要。

sentences.en: Research has shown that.
sentences.zh: 研究已经证明了这一点。

sentences.en: And there are some best practices that have been established through the years.
sentences.zh: 多年来已经建立了一些最佳实践。

sentences.en: If you look at an emergency room, for example, the best practice is that there should be four patients for every one nurse.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你看急诊室，最佳实践是每四名患者应配备一名护士。

sentences.en: So that way the nurse is not having too many patients that they are trying to monitor.
sentences.zh: 这样护士就不会因为要监测的患者太多而忙不过来。

sentences.en: And we were able to collect numbers showing the ratios in emergency rooms at private hospitals versus public hospitals.
sentences.zh: 我们收集的数据显示了私立医院与公立医院急诊室的比例。

sentences.en: And you could see that the ratios increased at every hospital.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到每家医院的比例都增加了。

sentences.en: But at the private hospitals, while the ratio went up to one nurse for six or seven patients, it went up at the public hospitals to one nurse for 10 or 15 or even 20 patients.
sentences.zh: 但在私立医院，比例上升到一名护士对应六到七名患者，而在公立医院，比例上升到一名护士对应10、15甚至20名患者。

sentences.en: So about twice.
sentences.zh: 大约是两倍。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in the ICUs, the general ratio is, because the patients are so severe, it's two patients for every nurse.
sentences.zh: 在重症监护室（ICU），通常的比例是，因为患者病情非常严重，每两名患者对应一名护士。

sentences.en: And again, those ratios got stretched at every hospital in the city.
sentences.zh: 同样，这些比例在全市每家医院都被拉伸了。

sentences.en: But in private hospitals, it would be stretched to three or four patients for every nurse.
sentences.zh: 但在私立医院，会被拉伸到每名护士对应三到四名患者。

sentences.en: And in the public hospitals, it was getting stretched to seven, eight, nine patients for every nurse, which was obviously very dangerous.
sentences.zh: 而在公立医院，被拉伸到每名护士对应七、八、九名患者，这显然非常危险。

sentences.en: And what did the staff you talked to say were the consequences in some of these public hospitals?
sentences.zh: 你交谈过的员工说，在这些公立医院中，后果是什么？

sentences.en: What did that translate into during the pandemic?
sentences.zh: 这在疫情期间意味着什么？

sentences.en: It meant that doctors and nurses had less time to spend with each patient in public hospitals to see how they were doing,
sentences.zh: 这意味着在公立医院，医生和护士花在每位患者身上的时间更少，无法观察他们的病情进展，

sentences.en: to talk with them, to run tests, and perhaps most importantly, just to monitor them.
sentences.zh: 无法与他们交谈，无法进行检查，也许最重要的是，无法持续监测他们。

sentences.en: Almost all of them were on ventilators and really needed to be constantly monitored.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎所有人都戴着呼吸机，确实需要持续监测。

sentences.en: One of the things that we've learned with the coronavirus is that patients can deteriorate very quickly.
sentences.zh: 我们从新冠病毒中学到的一件事是，患者的病情可能会迅速恶化。

sentences.en: They can seem like they're doing fine one minute, and the next minute they could be going into cardiac arreSt.
sentences.zh: 他们前一分钟看起来还好好的，下一分钟可能就会心脏骤停。

sentences.en: And at the understaffed public hospitals, we even heard some cases of patients waking up from medically induced comas,
sentences.zh: 在人员配备不足的公立医院，我们甚至听说过一些病例：患者从药物诱导的昏迷中醒来，

sentences.en: finding that there were no nurses around, and in their confusion, actually removing their life supports and dying.
sentences.zh: 发现周围没有护士，在神志不清的情况下，竟然拔掉了生命维持设备并死亡。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: It was something that was a pattern, so much of a pattern that at Elmhurst Hospital,
sentences.zh: 这是一种模式，这种模式在艾姆赫斯特医院（Elmhurst Hospital）非常普遍，

sentences.en: that overwhelmed hospital that received a lot of attention.
sentences.zh: 那家备受关注、不堪重负的医院。

sentences.en: This happens so often where somebody woke up, confused, and removed their life support because they needed to go to the bathroom,
sentences.zh: 这种情况经常发生，有人醒来后神志不清，因为想去洗手间而拔掉了生命维持设备，

sentences.en: and they collapsed, and they were discovered either in the bathroom or near the bathroom.
sentences.zh: 结果他们倒下了，被发现时要么在洗手间里，要么在洗手间附近。

sentences.en: Some of the doctors there actually developed a name for it.
sentences.zh: 那里的医生甚至为这种情况起了一个名字。

sentences.en: They called them bathroom codes.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“洗手间代码”。

sentences.en: And in those cases, the patients were discovered, you know, half an hour later, 45 minutes later,
sentences.zh: 在这些病例中，患者是在半小时、45分钟后才被发现的，

sentences.en: by doctors and nurses who were devastated because if there had been staff there monitoring them, they would have been cared for.
sentences.zh: 发现他们的医生和护士感到非常崩溃，因为如果有工作人员在那里监测他们，他们本可以得到照顾。

sentences.en: But instead a nurse was doing the rounds for 15 or 20 other patients.
sentences.zh: 但当时护士正在为其他15或20名患者查房。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And every case that we heard about, at least four cases at Elmhurst Hospital, the patients died.
sentences.zh: 在我们听说的每一个病例中，至少在艾姆赫斯特医院的四个病例中，患者都死亡了。

sentences.en: How else did the people you talked to in these hospitals tell you that staffing impacted mortality?
sentences.zh: 你交谈过的人还告诉你，人员配备如何影响了死亡率？

sentences.en: Well, another example is something called proning, which is quite simply flipping a patient on their stomach.
sentences.zh: 嗯，另一个例子是所谓的“俯卧位通气”，简单来说就是把患者翻转到腹部。

sentences.en: And it was something that very quickly during the pandemic, doctors realized that if they did,
sentences.zh: 在疫情期间，医生很快意识到，如果他们这样做，

sentences.en: if they flip patients on their stomach, it would help the patient breathe and could be a useful tool in helping them recover.
sentences.zh: 如果他们把患者翻转到腹部，将有助于患者呼吸，并可能成为帮助他们康复的有用工具。

sentences.en: And so that was something that was used a lot in New York in private hospitals.
sentences.zh: 所以这在纽约的私立医院被广泛使用。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, in public hospitals, there was not the staffing available to do it.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，在公立医院，没有足够的人手来做这件事。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Well, it turns out that proning, just flipping someone on their stomach can actually be quite complicated if they have a bunch of IV lines and tubes running through them.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，俯卧位通气，仅仅是把人翻转到腹部，如果他们身上插着一堆静脉输液管和导管，实际上可能非常复杂。

sentences.en: And it can require five or six people to coordinate all the movements and make sure those lines are still running while flipping the patient.
sentences.zh: 这可能需要五六个人来协调所有的动作，并确保在翻转患者时这些管子仍然通畅。

sentences.en: So it seems very simple, and the doctors knew that it would help, but in some of those public hospitals, they were not able to do it because they did not have the staff available.
sentences.zh: 所以这看起来很简单，医生们也知道这会有帮助，但在一些公立医院，他们无法做到，因为他们没有足够的人手。

sentences.en: One doctor at a small independent hospital told us that out of 10 of the deaths that he witnessed, he thought two or three of the patients could have been saved.
sentences.zh: 一家小型独立医院的一位医生告诉我们，在他目睹的10例死亡中，他认为有两三名患者本可以获救。

sentences.en: If there had been better staffing.
sentences.zh: 如果当时有更好的人员配备的话。

sentences.en: Yeah, if the hospital had the resources of a private hospital.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果那家医院拥有私立医院的资源。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: I mean, that's 20 to 30 percent.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是20%到30%。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it translates to thousands of people.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这相当于成千上万的人。

sentences.en: And we actually looked at the mortality rates at most of the 47 hospitals in the city.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上查看了全市47家医院中大多数医院的死亡率。

sentences.en: And in some cases, the mortality rate was three times higher in the public hospitals in the lower income areas.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，低收入地区的公立医院死亡率高出三倍。

sentences.en: Some of that mortality difference could be explained by differences in patient populations, you know, underlying health conditions of the patients.
sentences.zh: 部分死亡率差异可以用患者群体的差异来解释，你知道，患者潜在的健康状况。

sentences.en: But the experts and the doctors that we talked to said that the quality of care was definitely a factor in those differences.
sentences.zh: 但我们交谈过的专家和医生表示，护理质量绝对是造成这些差异的一个因素。

sentences.en: Brian, as horrible as everything you're describing is, it feels like there's a pretty logical solution to it, which is taking COVID-19 patients from these overburdened,
sentences.zh: 布莱恩，尽管你描述的一切都很可怕，但感觉有一个非常合乎逻辑的解决方案，那就是将新冠患者从这些负担过重、

sentences.en: understaffed public hospitals and transferring them to the less burdened, better staffed private hospitals.
sentences.zh: 人员配备不足的公立医院转移到负担较轻、人员配备更好的私立医院。

sentences.en: You'd think that, yes, and Governor Cuomo even said at the peak of the pandemic that that was going to happen.
sentences.zh: 你可能会这么想，是的，科莫州长在疫情高峰期甚至说过这种情况会发生。

sentences.en: How many beds will you need at the apex between 70 and 110,000?
sentences.zh: 在峰值时你需要多少张床位？7万到11万张之间？

sentences.en: Right now we have 53,000 statewide.
sentences.zh: 目前我们全州有5.3万张。

sentences.en: We have only 36,000 downstate.
sentences.zh: 我们在下州地区只有3.6万张。

sentences.en: Every hospital by mandate has to add a 50 percent increase.
sentences.zh: 每家医院按规定必须增加50%的容量。

sentences.en: And they have all done that.
sentences.zh: 他们都已经做到了。

sentences.en: We're setting up extra facilities.
sentences.zh: 我们正在建立额外的设施。

sentences.en: But in the end, it didn't.
sentences.zh: 但最终，并没有实现。

sentences.en: And why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Like, what prevents a patient at Elmhurst Hospital in Queens from being transferred to NYU Langone, which happens to be on the east side of Manhattan?
sentences.zh: 比如，是什么阻止了皇后区艾姆赫斯特医院的患者被转移到恰好位于曼哈顿东区的纽约大学朗格尼医学中心？

sentences.en: It's not that far.
sentences.zh: 距离并不远。

sentences.en: Well, Elmhurst is a public hospital.
sentences.zh: 嗯，艾姆赫斯特是一家公立医院。

sentences.en: And for decades, they have not really transferred patients to NYU Langone.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，他们并没有真正向纽约大学朗格尼医学中心转移患者。

sentences.en: They've transferred patients to other hospitals within the public system, but they just don't really work together with the private system.
sentences.zh: 他们会将患者转移到公立系统内的其他医院，但他们确实不与私立系统合作。

sentences.en: So there's no infrastructure set up to make such transfers, and therefore they're unlikely to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以没有建立进行此类转移的基础设施，因此它们不太可能发生。

sentences.en: Well, nothing physically prevents a patient from being transferred.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没有什么物理因素阻止患者被转移。

sentences.en: But first of all, the hospital, Elmhurst, may not want to transfer the patient because there is revenue attached to every patient.
sentences.zh: 但首先，艾姆赫斯特医院可能不想转移患者，因为每位患者都关联着收入。

sentences.en: Even a public hospital cares about maximizing its revenue.
sentences.zh: 即使是公立医院也关心最大化其收入。

sentences.en: So the doctor and the nurse inside the hospital may want very much to transfer a patient to Langone, but the administrator, the CEO of the hospital,
sentences.zh: 所以医院里的医生和护士可能非常想把患者转移到朗格尼，但医院的行政人员、首席执行官，

sentences.en: might not want to do that for financial reasons.
sentences.zh: 可能出于财务原因不想这样做。

sentences.en: So there's a problem on that end.
sentences.zh: 所以那一端存在问题。

sentences.en: And then there's a problem on the other end because NYU Langone is a private hospital,
sentences.zh: 然后另一端也存在问题，因为纽约大学朗格尼医学中心是一家私立医院，

sentences.en: and it wants to treat patients with private health insurance because that's going to bring the biggest profit.
sentences.zh: 它想治疗拥有私人健康保险的患者，因为那会带来最大的利润。

sentences.en: And the patient coming from Elmhurst, the public hospital, is going to be a patient without private health insurance.
sentences.zh: 而从公立医院艾姆赫斯特转来的患者，将是没有私人健康保险的患者。

sentences.en: So it's not a patient that NYU Langone really wants anyway.
sentences.zh: 所以无论如何，这都不是纽约大学朗格尼医学中心真正想要的患者。

sentences.en: So on both ends, Elmhurst may not want to transfer the patient, and NYU Langone might not want to take the patient.
sentences.zh: 所以两端都是如此，艾姆赫斯特可能不想转移患者，而纽约大学朗格尼医学中心可能不想接收患者。

sentences.en: So the incentives are not there for this very simple fix to work.
sentences.zh: 因此，这个非常简单的解决方案缺乏激励机制。

sentences.en: That's right, because the incentive is profit.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为激励机制是利润。

sentences.en: So at the end of the day, were there any transfers between the public and private hospitals?
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，公立和私立医院之间是否有过任何转移？

sentences.en: Any meaningful number of transfers?
sentences.zh: 有任何有意义的转移数量吗？

sentences.en: There were less than 50.
sentences.zh: 不到50例。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: During the whole course of the pandemic, thousands of people in hospitals, there were less than 50 transfers from public hospitals to private hospitals.
sentences.zh: 在整个疫情期间，医院里有成千上万的人，从公立医院到私立医院的转移不到50例。

sentences.en: That is a genuinely shocking number.
sentences.zh: 这是一个真正令人震惊的数字。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And again, the transfers were wanted by the doctors and the nurses, but they didn't end up happening.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，医生和护士都希望进行转移，但最终没有发生。

sentences.en: I'm very rarely shocked.
sentences.zh: 我很少感到震惊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That brings us to the other possible solution, which New York explored and actually poured a lot of money into, which was the overflow hospitals.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了另一种可能的解决方案，纽约曾对此进行过探索，实际上还投入了大量资金，那就是溢出医院。

sentences.en: Makeshift hospitals set up around the city that could take patients from these overburdened hospitals.
sentences.zh: 在城市各处设立临时医院，接收那些不堪重负的医院里的病人。

sentences.en: But it turns out those didn't work either.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，这些方法也不奏效。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: It's going to help take the pressure off ElmhurSt.

sentences.zh: 但它遇到的第一个问题是官僚主义。

sentences.en: And they were conveying different directives to other hospitals about which types of patients they should be transferring to the Billie Jean King Tennis Center.
sentences.zh: 有超过25种不同的排除标准，基本上就是一些取消资格的条件，如果病人有这些情况，就不能去比利·简·金网球中心。

sentences.en: And they ended up crafting a series of rules that were very restrictive about the types of patients that could go to Billie Jean King.

sentences.en: There were over 25 different exclusionary criteria, which is basically disqualifying conditions that if the patient has, they can't go to Billie Jean King.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，还有一系列关于他们不接收哪类病人的规则，因为这些病人的病情不够严重。

sentences.en: And one of them was just the fact that the patient had a fever, which is a hallmark symptom of the coronavirus.

sentences.en: But at the same time, there were also a series of rules about the types of patients that they would not see because they were not severe enough.

sentences.en: There were patients that were quarantining with the virus in hotels and in some cases ended up dying in those hotels.

sentences.en: Well, hold on, because there's another problem and it relates to ambulances.

sentences.en: but there was no ambulance available to transfer them.
sentences.zh: 他们本可以去医院接病人。

sentences.en: And Billie Jean King had its own ambulances on site.

sentences.en: They could have gone to the hospital and picked up the patient.

In the end, how many patients made it into this Billie Jean King overflow hospital?

sentences.en: Well, in many cases, nothing.

sentences.en: You know, I want to be clear because the doctors and nurses and other staffers that came to work at Billie Jean King, they came in many cases from around the country.

sentences.en: I felt really ashamed, to be honeSt.

sentences.zh: 将病人从公立医院转移到私立医院。

sentences.en: You know, cancel those exclusive ambulance agreements.
sentences.zh: 这些似乎都在可控范围内。

sentences.en: Transfer patients from public to private hospitals.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想你是对的。

sentences.en: They all seem quite within reach.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为值得注意的是，即使在疫情期间，

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 也有很多医生和其他医院工作人员注意到了这些不平等现象，并试图解决它们。

sentences.en: And I think it's also important to note that even while the pandemic was going on,
sentences.zh: 我们采访了一些医生，他们实际上在私立医院和公立医院之间轮岗，并试图敲响警钟，甚至私立网络内的医院也在试图推动他们的老板做更多工作来解决不平等问题。

sentences.en: there were plenty of doctors and other hospital workers who noticed these inequalities and were trying to fix them.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，到那时，不平等已经深深植根于医院系统中，他们能做的并不多。

sentences.en: We talked with a number of doctors that actually rotated between working in the private hospitals and working in the public hospitals and were trying to raise alarms and even hospitals within the private networks trying to push their bosses to do more to address inequalities.
sentences.zh: 我认为新冠疫情高峰期纽约医院发生的故事，实际上是关于官员、医院高管和官僚们的故事，

sentences.en: But the reality was, by that point, the inequalities were so ingrained into the hospital system that there wasn't a whole lot that they could do.
sentences.zh: 他们很久以前就接受了系统中的这些不平等，显然几十年来一直知道这些不平等，

sentences.en: I think the story of what happened in hospitals in New York in the height of the coronavirus pandemic is really a story about officials and hospital executives and bureaucrats
sentences.zh: 但选择不去解决它们，结果发现它们在这次疫情中暴露无遗。

sentences.en: who accepted these inequalities in the system long ago and have obviously known about inequalities for decades,
sentences.zh: 但当然，在这种情况下，这难道不是政府的职责吗？

sentences.en: but chose not to address them and found that they got exposed in this pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这难道不是纽约市市长、

sentences.en: But of course, in that case, isn't it the role of government?
sentences.zh: 纽约州州长的职责吗？不去接受那种不平等，并尽其所能打破公共卫生危机中的那种自满情绪？

sentences.en: Isn't it the role of the mayor of New York City,
sentences.zh: 是的，我想如果你和州长或市长交谈，如果你让他们坐在这里，他们会说他们已经尽力了。

sentences.en: the governor of New York to not accept those kinds of inequalities and to do everything in their power to slice through that kind of complacency in the midst of a public health crisis?
sentences.zh: 他们确实花了很多钱建立方舱医院来提供帮助，并建立了一个系统来帮助转院。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think if you talk to the governor or the mayor, if you had them sitting here, they would say that they did as much as they could.
sentences.zh: 但我认为有一件事非常能说明问题，那就是当我打电话给州长办公室询问为什么没有更多的病人从不堪重负的医院转移到有空床位的私立医院时，

sentences.en: And they did certainly spend a lot of money setting up field hospitals to help and set up a system to help with transfers.
sentences.zh: 州长办公室说，他们满足了医院提出的每一项转院请求，他们觉得这就是他们的工作。

sentences.en: But one thing that I think is very telling is when I called the governor's office to ask why more patients were not transferred from overburdened hospitals to private hospitals that had open beds.
sentences.zh: 所以他们处理了每一个请求，但他们不愿意强迫医院进行转院。

sentences.en: The governor's office said that the governor's office said that they accommodated every transfer that was requested by the hospitals, and they felt like that was their job.
sentences.zh: 他们不愿意在改变政府角色方面迈出更根本的一步。

sentences.en: So they handled each request, but they were not willing to force hospitals to transfer.
sentences.zh: 我想这是因为他们自己接受了现实，即不同类型的医院和不同类型的病人之间必然存在不平等。

sentences.en: They were not willing to take that more fundamental step in changing the government's role.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think it's because they themselves kind of accepted the reality as it was that there were going to be inequalities between different types of hospitals and different types of patients.
sentences.zh: 说他们处理了收到的每一个转院请求，就像是说，我在这场巨大的风暴中接住了几滴雨点，但街上的洪水又该怎么办呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: To say that they processed every request they got for transfer is to say, like, I caught a couple of the raindrops in this giant storm, but what about that flood down the street?
sentences.zh: 这并没有解决更根本的问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩，在谈话开始时，你提到住院人数的高峰现在正在全国大部分地区出现。

sentences.en: It's not addressing the more fundamental problem.
sentences.zh: 在纽约已经平息了，但现在正在德克萨斯州发生。

sentences.en: Brian, at the start of our conversation, you mentioned that peak hospitalizations are now occurring throughout much of the rest of the country.
sentences.zh: 正在佛罗里达州发生。

sentences.en: It's subsided in New York, but it's now happening in Texas.
sentences.zh: 正在亚利桑那州发生。

sentences.en: It's happening in Florida.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's happening in Arizona.
sentences.zh: 我知道你的调查是针对纽约的医院，但我们是否预期你在纽约看到的情况，这些不平等，这些私立与公立医院的差距，

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 很可能会在全国其他地区重演？

sentences.en: I know that your investigation was into the hospitals in New York, but do we expect that what you saw in New York, these inequities, these private-public hospital disparities,
sentences.zh: 美国每个城市肯定都会存在差距。

sentences.en: that they are likely to play out across the rest of the country?
sentences.zh: 我认为问题在于其他城市是否从纽约吸取了教训，并愿意实施能够以比我们在纽约看到的更真实的方式平衡这些不平等的系统和政策。

sentences.en: There will definitely be disparities in every city in America.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一点还有待观察。

sentences.en: I think the question is whether other cities have learned from New York and are going to be willing to put in place systems and policies that can help balance out those inequalities in a more real way than we saw in New York.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: And I think that's still to be determined.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Brian, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: On Sunday, The Times reported that the total number of infections in Florida has now surpassed that of New York, making the state the new epicenter of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 《泰晤士报》周日报道称，佛罗里达州的感染总数现已超过纽约州，成为疫情新的中心。

sentences.en: Florida has nearly 424,000 reported cases, compared with about 415,000 cases in New York.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州报告的病例数接近42.4万例，而纽约州约为41.5万例。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to end their day.
sentences.zh: 以下是你结束这一天还需要了解的内容。

sentences.en: The Times reports that the presence of federal agents in Portland galvanized thousands of people to join protests across the country over the weekend,
sentences.zh: 《泰晤士报》报道称，联邦特工在波特兰的出现促使周末全国各地成千上万的人加入抗议活动，

sentences.en: reviving nationwide protests that had largely dissipated.
sentences.zh: 使原本已基本平息的全国性抗议活动重新燃起。

sentences.en: One of the most intense protests was in Seattle, where a demonstration against police brutality turned violent after some protesters lit a detention center on fire,
sentences.zh: 最激烈的抗议活动之一发生在西雅图，一场反对警察暴力的示威活动在一些抗议者点燃了一处拘留中心后演变为暴力事件，

sentences.en: smashed windows, and damaged a police building.
sentences.zh: 他们砸碎窗户，并破坏了一座警察大楼。

sentences.en: In response, police declared the protest a riot, fired flash grenades, unleashed pepper spray, and rushed into crowds, knocking people to the ground.
sentences.zh: 作为回应，警方宣布此次抗议为骚乱，发射了闪光弹，使用了胡椒喷雾，并冲入人群，将人们撞倒在地。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我和莎拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》节目。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在你收听播客的任何平台收听。

sentences.en: Let's see you next time.
sentences.zh: 我们下次见。
